quest.title: Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand
quest.description: The merchants and their Sumpter Beasts waiting in the oasis might be in danger. Hurry back to the camp in the oasis to secure Nachtigal's safety.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Wonderful, Cyrus seems to be in a good mood. Windwheel Aster's looking good too.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: It got the name Windwheel Aster because it kept spinning on the ground after knocking some kegs over... I wanted to name it Keg, but Bonifaz was of the opinion that it wasn't a nice name.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: "Since we have Dandelion, it makes sense to have Windwheel Aster, right?" is what he said.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: I know he's my friend, but I really can't compliment his taste in names.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Benben, stop running off with bad people. Once Tirzad has uncovered all the secrets here, he can head back and write his masterpiece... And you can come home with me and father.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Just like how Paimon stays with {NICKNAME}, I'm sure you and I will be best companions. Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: I'm just so happy that you're all alright too. *sigh* They really came at us. Luckily, Jebrael gave us some instructions beforehand, so they didn't make things too difficult for us.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: If Bonifaz had Jebrael's wisdom, then perhaps our business would be doing much better than it currently is.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: You think too highly of him, then. Wisdom? He's one of them. I'll bet it's experience talking!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father wouldn't do something like that!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: There's no need to argue with him, Jeht. It's my fault.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I don't care what happened in the past! As far as I'm concerned, you have nothing to do with Samail now, and that's enough for me!

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: What's going on? I thought a night in the oasis might bring all of you closer together. Why are you at each other's throats again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's a long story...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Nachtigal everything...

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: ...I see. But I don't have the right to comment on it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Well, that's because Tirzad is the one who's paying me. No matter who I support, I'll be in a difficult spot.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: If I support Jebrael, Tirzad will probably scream at me to get lost.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: But if I support Tirzad, then we'll be without Jebrael in this world of sand and bandits...

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, what would you do in a situation like this?

choices.text: Tirzad's words are not without merit...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon really wants to believe Jebrael, but he hasn't told us much about his past either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That weird guy popped up and claimed to be his old companion, but Jebrael didn't even deny it...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There can be no trust without honesty.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, if you'd just tell us the truth, Jebrael, Paimon believes that everyone can be understanding!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, Jeht's his daughter. Paimon really can't imagine someone who raised Jeht as being a bad guy...

response.speaker: Nachtigal
response.text: Hmm, I believe that the most important thing right now is to get Tirzad to trust Jebrael.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: What? You're a merchant. You should know the value of trust! Even in the world of academics, researchers who engage in misconduct will be stripped of their research qualifications.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Just ask yourself, would you trade with someone who cheated you in the past?

response.speaker: Nachtigal
response.text: Oh, about that... I would decide based on the circumstances. Haha, I dare not speak for others, but Bonifaz and I have much more flexible moral standards.

response.speaker: Nachtigal
response.text: After weighing the risks and the benefits, we usually choose to take the risk. We wouldn't have accepted your commission otherwise.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Ugh, you guys!

response.speaker: Nachtigal
response.text: I think I said this before, but you sure are stubborn. Forget about Samail for a moment and ask yourself a question. Has Jebrael ever done anything to harm you?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: ...No, I don't think so.

response.speaker: Nachtigal
response.text: Then hasn't he proven himself through his actions?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know, when you caused all that commotion after getting drunk, it was Jebrael who stayed and took care of you, Tirzad.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This isn't the time for fighting amongst ourselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we haven't even found the place marked on the map yet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jebrael is definitely the person in our group who knows the most about the desert. It'll be difficult for our expedition to proceed without him leading the way.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: #...Fine! I'll do it for you. I know I can trust you two, Paimon, {NICKNAME}. I'll trust you again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright! The Tirzad Archaeological Team is back together again!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: We still have time. We should travel to the next oasis and rest there in preparation for the next leg of this expedition.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: I... I'm willing to explain, to repay you for your trust. But the journey is our current priority.

choices.text: I think Jebrael has changed his ways.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't think Jebrael's a bad guy either. Anyway, that guy Samail has a weird way of speaking! It's best not to believe everything he says.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Jebrael is his enemy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, so they're definitely not on the same side.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Samail is watching us, so we aren't safe right now. I may not want to admit it, but he knows me just as well as I know him.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: There's a lot to discuss, but let's set up camp first.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and everyone else set up the camp in silence. It is already getting dark as you finish your meal...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Now that our bellies are full, what other excuses do you have? Let's hear them! And what did you slip to Nachtigal earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: You'd better not be thinking of using the merchants to send messages to the enemy!

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Tirzad, you're being too hostile. No one's going to talk if you act like that.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: It was just a note on some trivial matters. It's with the luggage that you won't be able to take with you. You can have it once you return safely.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: He can be hostile all he wants. I'm angry too! Forget Tirzad, even I've never heard about my father's past!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I refuse to believe he's an evil person, but it's his secretiveness that caused all of this.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: None of this would have happened if he told us everything from the beginning! Ugh! Now I don't even know where to start.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe we should start with his relationship with Samail?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Exactly! I can't sleep in peace without getting to the bottom of that...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: All of you heard Samail, yes? Well, he was telling the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Just like him, I was a member of the Eremite band named "Thutmose." However, I betrayed him and Thutmose both.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Did you do it because of mother?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: N—No, that's not it. I thought I'd never have to mention this to anyone ever again... In the end, it was all my fault.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: There were ill feelings between me and Samail, but I only regarded myself as an insignificant grain of sand. I did as Thutmose needed of me.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Ufairah was a capable researcher, and the Thutmose coveted her wisdom. They hoped to use her knowledge to solve the puzzle Al-Ahmar left behind.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: So, I "invited" her to the desert and explored many ruins with her.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Our years spent exploring together did bear some fruit. But... it wasn't enough for Thutmose.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: And was Jeht included in those "results"?

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Ahem! Come on, Tirzad, some things are best left unsaid.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I'm making a reasonable inference here...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: ...As I said, there were ill feelings between Samail and me.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: After Jeht was born, I kept asking myself if I could still wholeheartedly carry out the missions Thutmose gave me as I had been doing in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Could I still tolerate what Samail was doing?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: In the end, Ufairah and I decided to use hitting a bottleneck in her research as an excuse to take Jeht away from the desert, and away from Thutmose.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: But Samail saw through my weakness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! It can't be...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: A researcher that can't unlock the secrets of Al-Ahmar is worthless to Thutmose...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: He even thought that I would have no reason to leave Thutmose once Ufairah was gone.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I... What...! How do you even sleep at night after witnessing things like that?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: I... I do my best.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So our encounter with Samail was a coincidence?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Yes... and no. Thutmose will never give up an opportunity to unlock Al-Ahmar's secrets. I thought that we might encounter them, but I never expected that we would run into Samail.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those Fatui too! Paimon wonders what wicked plots they and Samail are hatching together!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: He will stop at nothing to achieve his objectives. That's the kind of person Samail is.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then what's your goal on this trip, Jebrael?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: My goal?

response.speaker: Nachtigal
response.text: Honestly, I wouldn't be surprised if he was here for the Mora! After all, someone like Tirzad who's foolish and rich... *cough* Uh, I mean generous, is pretty hard to come by.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: I'm not drunk, you know! I heard it all!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Perhaps it's as Jeht said. Coming to the desert is like returning home, and in the end, I'm a grain of sand. I was born here, and I shall be buried here as well.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Ufairah and I were like a bird and a fish, but Al-Ahmar's secrets allowed our fates to intertwine. Now, you and I, people from different lands, are again here for those very same secrets.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: I didn't mention all of this to you because it was my own selfish dream, and it had nothing to do with Jeht. I didn't want to make her bear any burdens she doesn't have to.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Tirzad, we hold different opinions on Al-Ahmar, but you are one of the researchers from the Hindi Clan. As long as we reach the throne...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...The throne?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Our destination tomorrow, Khaj-Nisut, is where Al-Ahmar's throne lies. According to the legends of the desert, only the chosen are worthy to kneel before the throne...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: The times have changed. If I have a chance to look upon the Golden Slumber that Al-Ahmar promised... I'll be able to fulfill the lifelong wish that Ufairah and I share.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: To that end, I will do as we agreed and protect you to the end.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: #Hmm... alright. Our side would be the weaker by far if it were just {NICKNAME} and me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! How could you forget about Paimon!?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: I don't think you can be included in any estimation of our group's strength.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! Paimon's definitely stronger than you, though!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Anyway, I have new worries now... Jebrael, don't you have revenge on your mind at all? I know you've repeatedly promised to protect me until the commission is over, but...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: The loss of your wife isn't something you can just laugh off, is it...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: If we meet him again... No, I think we definitely will. Even I know that he'll be waiting in ambush for us at our final destination.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: At that time, what will your priority be? Will you take a step forward to get revenge, or step back to keep us safe?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, Tirzad! Stop putting people on the spot like that!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: It's a very realistic question! And it's linked to my survival, so of course I have to pursue an answer...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: If taking revenge on Samail could bring Ufairah back to life... A good deal like that...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: ...Even if I had to gut him ten times... even a hundred times! I wouldn't hesitate at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Hah, but this is a meaningless delusion that even Al-Ahmar would pay no attention to. I can only pray she has found peace amidst the endless ocean of sand...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: A man chained by hatred cannot raise a daughter.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: That's why I left the sands behind me, so that Jeht could get away from all of this... and those feelings that will not edify her.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Father... I—I didn't know anything. I even said that you did all this because you couldn't forget the desert and the hot winds here...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: If you hate it here, let's just leave right now! Forget Samail...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: To be honest, I want to know about the past, I want to know how you and mother met each other and fell in love, I want to know what you and mother had been through, the sweet memories and everything else...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But... if bringing up these memories will bring you sorrow, then I'd rather not hear about them. Just leave them buried here!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I'll stop liking the sand, and I'll stop treating this place as home...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: We've been together since I can remember. Nothing in this world is more important to me than you... So long as you're well, we can be at home anywhere...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Wait, wait, you can't leave! Our expedition isn't over yet!

choices.text: But you were sooo suspicious of them just a while ago...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Th—things change! I fully trust Jebrael now. He certainly isn't on Samail's side, at least. Uh, he isn't, right?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Don't worry, I won't quit halfway.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Perhaps a day will come when I shall meet her again in the Eternal Oasis.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: When that day comes, spring water will replace salt water, joy will wash away the pain, roses will never wither, and the feasts will never end...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: But that day is still very, very far away. It will definitely not be now... She knows that I have a mission to complete.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: I will assist you in unlocking the secrets of Al-Ahmar and protect you until the end. Samail will not obstruct us, because I will clear him out of your way.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: As for Ufairah... If I have the chance, I'll tell you everything, Jeht. Time will gradually filter away the bitter impurities... though I'm not good with words.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: ...I may not be able to even convey a thousandth of her beautiful qualities. But if you're willing to listen... I will tell you everything I know.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: M—My head's a mess. Father, can you sing that song again? "O stars high above the wasteland..." It always calms me.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: It's a song that Ufairah deciphered from Al-Ahmar's texts.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: "O stars high above the wasteland, O nightingales weary from the day. It's time to take off the crown of roses; Cleanse yourself with wine made from grapes."

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: I'll take the night watch. Don't stay up too late.

response.speaker: Black Screen

choices.text: You really have a way with words, don't you?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: You think so? You should read my papers. I reckon I'm much better at writing than speaking!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even Paimon knows that wasn't a compliment!

choices.text: Are you still unable to let go of King Deshret's secrets?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But Jebrael said that even years of research with Ufairah amounted to nothing... So how would relying on Tirzad really change anything...?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Why wouldn't you believe in my skills? Listen, we're going to fill in the blanks tomorrow. In truth, I already know how I'm going to write my paper!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Phew... We're finally here.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But... Is the alcohol still clouding my mind, or has the sand distorted my vision? Is this really the place we're looking for? I can see Khaj-Nisut... but it feels like I also don't.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Actually, I've been meaning to ask... You clearly can't hold your alcohol, so why are you so fond of drinking?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep... Bee-eep?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: ...I'd hoped it would prove my fountain of wisdom, but it makes my world spin instead. Ugh... You're right, I really should slow down a little.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But I'll be fine. Nachtigal gave me some invigorating drinks before we left, so I'm as clear-headed as can be.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It feels like we're missing a little something here.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: "Just a little" might be an understatement. Khaj-Nisut is where it should be, but it seems to be refusing to show itself to us...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And what's that supposed to mean?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Shh, look over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's the Eremites! They got here before us...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Huh? What should we do? Avoid them?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: No, let's go have a little "chat" with them.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But we didn't get along the last time, and we even fought each other. Can we even talk to them now?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Haha! Tirzad, do you think we're going over there to invite them for tea?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: We're going to communicate in our own way, of course! And if all else fails, we'll "talk" with our fists. It is what my father and I are best at.

dialogues.speaker: Eremite Mercenary
dialogues.text: Who are you? Hah! The researcher and the traitor? Good! Give us the stuff Samail mentioned!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Give you what? We don't owe you anything!

dialogues.speaker: Eremite Mercenary
dialogues.text: Hmph! Acting dumb won't save you! Take this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Well, looks like negotiations have broken down!

dialogues.speaker: Omid
dialogues.text: Okay, I've made up my mind! I'm going to Port Ormos. I haven't yet decided on what business to go into, but I'll figure that out after seeing what other people are doing there.

dialogues.speaker: Omid
dialogues.text: I'll inform the boss once I'm back in Aaru Village. Although he always complains that he's short on crew, I guess he'll be alright with Mirsad to help him.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: How strange... It feels like they didn't go all out. What did they mean when they mentioned Samail's orders?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it about Benben? Benben did get taken away before.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Bee-eep!? Beep...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hmm, it is possible. Besides Tirzad, we must protect Benben well too.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: They probably stayed for a while. Let's look around, there might still be some clues.

talks.objective: Search for clues in the Eremites' camp

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jebrael! We found this, though we're not sure if it's a useful clue...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: When I was still with the Thutmose, we used to leave messages for each other in code just like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! So you can read it, Jebrael?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Samail should be aware that he can.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Th—Then is all of this a trap that Samail set for us?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I knew your past would come back to bite us...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: *sigh* Come on, Benben, why don't we just return to Sumeru City now? It is quite regrettable that my paper won't have its final two chapters, but I can always return again if I'm still alive.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Next time, I should get help that has a clean background...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: We can use this against them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: We're the latecomers here. They've been here for quite some time, and they've made some discoveries, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: They just lack something crucial, so they can't advance.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: And we just happen to have what they need.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Yes, and the stone slate.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Instead of taking them from us, they have a better way to get what they want.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh, so they'd like to sit back and claim the fruits of our work?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Yes, they'd prefer it if we solved everything for them.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Oh! I get it! They're the people in joint research projects that contribute nothing but take all the credit when it's time to present your findings!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: But they won't be able to get what they want if we get stuck here too.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: So, we can use this against them.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: #...We can't avoid a fight once everything has been uncovered. But Jeht, {NICKNAME}, neither of you will run from a fight, right?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Of course. I've decided to punch that guy in the face when we meet again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we've fought worse.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Sorry to interrupt... But there must be a safer method, right?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Just think about it, the ruins have been here for years, so just a few months... or even a few years won't change anything! We can come back later!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: *sigh* Using their plan against them is a bad idea. All four of you do seem so full of confidence, but that's because you're skilled fighters.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: But there are just too many of them. Paimon can fly away and hide if things go south, but what about me?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: For safety's sake, we should return to Sumeru City and draw up a plan... No, even Aaru Village would be fine!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Those Thutmose folks may believe in King Deshret, but that doesn't mean they won't touch the ruins. If he can't do it through ordinary means, Samail will use other means...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: If they solve King Deshret's puzzle before us, these ruins probably won't be the same when you return, Tirzad.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: What!? But they're all relics!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: They may be precious relics to you researchers from the Akademiya, but they clearly aren't to the Thutmose. It's all just a process, a phase...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: They only care about the final objective... Results are what matters to them.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Tirzad, do you still not get it? We have no other choice now.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: *sob* It saddens me to think that I won't get to celebrate my success because I'll have to face the fangs of that venomous snake who will leap out of the shadows...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: He may be in the shadows, but we're prepared for him. I won't let him touch you.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: According to this coded letter, Al-Ahmar's throne only shows itself to the worthy who have passed the three trials.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The three trials... Maybe that refers to the buildings all around us? Y'know, there are so many huge statues here, Paimon's worried that they'll just come to life...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe the trial is to defeat them.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: I can only hope that you're wrong...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alrighty then! Forward it is!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: That's right.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Well, it does make sense that they can't advance without the guidance of a professional like me, yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Oh? Is that really how it is?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: We wouldn't have been able to approach the core without Tirzad's stone slate and Benben.

talks.objective: Report back to Jebrael on the discovered clues

dialogues.speaker: Mirsad
dialogues.text: *sigh* Am I too old to start a new career as an adventurer now? That being said, I won't know until I try.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsad
dialogues.text: Omid'll definitely take me for a madman if I tell him. That's why I'd better only inform my boss. Please keep the secret for me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we're obviously inside... But where's the throne?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Why would you think the throne would be facing the entrance? It isn't a receptionist's desk. Hmm, actually, I feel like I shouldn't say such... Uh, disrespectful things in a place like this.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Anyway, King Deshret's throne should be in a more "dignified" place, or in simpler terms, a place that's higher up.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: The mechanisms here probably stopped working a long time ago. We've got to find a way to reactivate them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh... Paimon can't wait to see what the throne looks like.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everything linked to King Deshret is huge! So that throne is definitely very, very huge, right? Hehe, Paimon wants to take a seat on it!

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Bee-eep? Beep...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Something seems to be the matter with Benben. It seems like... it wants to go down?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But Tirzad said the throne is definitely higher up...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Hmm... to go up, we must first go down. You cannot reach a peak without falling to your lowest, just like...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just like in life.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Yes! Exactly! Hah, looks like you've learned quite a bit these past few days you spent with me, eh?

talks.objective: Activate Plinth(s) of the Secret Rites
Activate the mechanism in the center of the hall
Activate the mechanism in the center of the hall
Activate the mechanism in the center of the hall
Activate the mechanism in the center of the hall
Operate Prism of Khaj-Nisut and try to reach Khaj-Nisut's upper floor

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, this chair is huge! Paimon feels like just sitting on it is gonna make Paimon super great!

choices.text: I want to sit on it too.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: I may disapprove of a tyrant like King Deshret, but your thoughts might be a little too audacious even so, Paimon...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Anyway, nothing happened. Huh? Is something lacking? Or perhaps we made a mistake somewhere...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Hmm... Jebrael did mention that only the chosen may kneel before the throne... M—Maybe we really have to kneel before the throne?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: But I'm a researcher of the Akademiya. I can't kneel before a tyrant's throne! And it's an empty throne, too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, it won't be empty once Paimon sits there.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: You're seriously... Jeht, please, help me with Paimon... Jeht?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Wait. Where did Jeht go? She was still with us just a moment ago, right?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Samail...

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Jebrael, are you still refusing to admit that you are a Thutmose deep down? Self-deceiving makes no difference for people like us, you know it!

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Al-Ahmar's throne is right before us. Aren't you obsessed with it too?

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: No mere grain of sand can reject the Golden Slumber. Al-Ahmar's promise is the paradise that all of us dream of.

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Did you think betraying the Thutmose would be enough to deny your nature? Hah! I knew you would be back.

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Little Jeht, do you see it now? Once he laid eyes on Al-Ahmar's throne, your dear father forgot everything! Even you!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: That was my mistake. It has nothing to do with him!

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Hmph! You're just as stubborn as your father, but your talkativeness... I guess you must've gotten that from Ufairah, huh?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Samail, we've solved everything for you and brought you to the throne. Your dream... should be fulfilled. Jeht is useless to you, so why keep her?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: I see! So you're finally showing your true colors, huh, Jebrael? "Use their plans against them"? You're just one of them, like I expected!

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Hahahaha! So this is your choice? Looks like your companions never really trusted you at all.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Tirzad, your expedition should be over now. We've explored the entire Khaj-Nisut, and you now have all the knowledge you need for your paper...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: We should start considering how to get back safely now... I promised to protect you until the end, and I'll keep my word.

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Tsk tsk tsk! Such greed!

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Jebrael, I thought I knew you... But I really don't understand what you're doing right now.

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: You're trying to shoulder every burden! Your daughter's safety! That researcher's commission! And even Al-Ahmar's secrets!

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: I thought you learned your lesson about greed when Ufairah died! Oh, sorry, or should I say "I taught you that lesson when Ufairah died"?

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Oh! Perhaps you learned your lesson, and you're prepared to pay the price now? Let's see which one amongst them will be the price you pay!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This weirdo keeps saying weird stuff. Paimon's getting confused... Haven't we uncovered everything? And what are Al-Ahmar's secrets, anyway?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And the Golden Slumber...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Aren't those just desert superstitions? Things like that are... too vague. There's no research value in them.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: They say anyone who gains King Deshret's wisdom is permitted to enter the Golden Slumber, and enjoy eternal peace and happiness there.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Besides ignorant children... who could take that seriously?

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Hmph! You third-rate researcher! Oh, if Ufairah were alive, she would have written multiple books by now! Someone like you has no right to talk about Al-Ahmar's legacy.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: ...Enough! If you wish to sit on Al-Ahmar's throne, then do as you please. I won't stop you, and I won't let Tirzad do that either.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: #I opened the path to Al-Ahmar's throne for you, and I used Tirzad and {NICKNAME} to make Khaj-Nisut manifest itself.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: I don't think I owe Tirzad anything. He wanted a paper that could shock the academic world, and now he has material that no one else has. I've helped him accomplish his objective.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Now, give Jeht to me, and we'll be even.

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Hmm. I'm really curious. Why are you always so evasive whenever Al-Ahmar's secrets are mentioned?

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: It's an empty throne! Anyone can sit on it. An unqualified and mediocre person won't become great just by sitting on it...

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: That prayer is the key... But of course you know that! Hmm... Well, it all makes sense if you were planning to return alone.

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: Unfortunately, unless you're willing to pay with little Jeht's life...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Nothing is more important than family.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Paimon may not know what the secrets of Al-Ahmar he keeps mentioning are... But it doesn't matter if it's the truth, or if it's superstition like Tirzad says...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Both strength and endless wealth are nothing before family!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: What kind of prayer has that much appeal...? I refuse to believe it. But I don't mind listening in. It wouldn't hurt to include it as an anecdote in my paper.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: If something like that can be exchanged for Jeht's safety, then stop hesitating and tell him.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: To be honest, I expected that we might have to fight for our lives to get home... So isn't it great that we can resolve this peacefully?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: I never expected to see such intense superstition... I guess my knowledge is still lacking. Perhaps this superstition, linked to King Deshret as it is, may be worth studying after all.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: "O stars high above the wasteland..."

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Jebrael recites the song he sang softly at night in the oasis.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: But isn't this...?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...Father?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Jebrael? Why?)

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: (Get ready.)

response.speaker: Samail
response.text: "O stars high above the wasteland," huh? I see.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Samail repeats the "prayer."

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: ...What is this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, he looks so strange! He fell asleep... No, wait! He isn't breathing!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: He got what he wanted. He's inside the Golden Slumber that Al-Ahmar promised, the Eternal Dreamland...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So that's what you meant by the Eternal Dreamland?

response.speaker: Eremite Mercenary
response.text: What happened to Samail? None of you will leave this place alive!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, get ready for battle!

choices.text: Sitting on a seat that doesn't belong to you won't end well.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father! What's going on? That prayer...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Jebrael, you mentioned that Jeht's mother deciphered it from Al-Ahmar's texts... I didn't expect it to be used here...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But... Is Al-Ahmar's Golden Slumber a way to send his believers into eternal sleep?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: That makes it more terrifying than I ever imagined... I really should get back and update the collective knowledge of the academic world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek, thank goodness Paimon didn't sit on that throne... Guess sitting on a seat that doesn't belong to you really doesn't end well, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have so many questions...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Ufairah made this inference about Al-Ahmar's promise...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Those who offer the correct prayer to Al-Ahmar will be granted entry into the Golden Slumber, but it's a one way trip.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: No one can move freely between the Eternal Dreamland and reality. It seems like Ufairah was right. Samail is gone forever.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: I must admit that it was a very risky gamble...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But all that matters is Jeht is safe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Everyone's safe, and that's the most important thing!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me summarize the overall situation now... Jeht's back safely, and Samail's subordinates have been defeated.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Samail... He got his wish, didn't he? If he wasn't such a villain, I'd even feel like thanking him...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Anyway, uh, since he's in the paradise he dreamed of, I don't need his permission to use him as a case study in my paper, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: ...Hah, all's well that ends well, eh? I, Tirzad, hereby announce that this archaeological expedition has been completed successfully and has yielded great results!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: ...Is it really over? This doesn't feel real...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Actually, it isn't over. I mean, the minimum requirement in the commission was to escort me safely back to Aaru Village, right?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hmm, that's true. Tirzad's commission isn't over, so I can't slack off just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father and I will be free once we escort Tirzad back safely! Hehe, then we can go wherever we want.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh! I'm not talking about the desert, by the way. I mean literally anywhere!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: It's fine, Jeht. I'm willing to accompany you wherever you want to go. As for Ufairah... I'll tell you about her, if you're willing to listen.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: There's her research notes too... But I don't know if you'll be interested in those.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: I was worried about losing them, so I didn't bring them along. I left them and some luggage with Bonifaz. Once we return to Aaru Village and get our luggage...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Well, what are we waiting for? Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Does anyone else feel like something's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Something's coming this way!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What's going on? How could this be?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Bee-eep! Beep...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Is it Samail...? Oh no! If he gained Al-Ahmar's wisdom, then even if it's just for an instant, he would have gained Al-Ahmar's authority...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: We must leave immediately!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: We must leave immediately!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The door's closed again? Thank goodness, we made it out in time...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Jebrael... protected us, but he... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: *sob* Father...

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep... Beep-boop beep... Bee-eep...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It must be Jebrael who opened the door for us. Without him, we would've been...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He fulfilled his promise...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: This place may not be completely safe... Let's meet up with Nachtigal's group and head back to Aaru Village...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
Refusing to give up, Jeht examined the entrance to Khaj-Nisut time after time, only to find the door tightly shut.
Behind it was dead silence. Things had happened and were beyond redemption.
Jeht, now having but to accept reality, put away Jebrael's axe carefully. It is the only thing he has left behind.
We finally managed to persuade her to come back with us to the camp. We then informed the merchants of what happened and returned to Aaru Village...

dialogues.speaker: Bonifaz
dialogues.text: To think that something like that happened... Anemo Archon bless us all...

dialogues.speaker: Bonifaz
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm really sorry about what happened to Jebrael. But at least all of you returned safely.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: I think we may have to reconsider our career as traveling merchants... The desert is a hundred times more dangerous than I expected... Even someone as capable as Jebrael...

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: A nobody like me doesn't have that many lives! Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Bonifaz
dialogues.text: This may be bad timing, but I have to ask about what all of you plan to do now...

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: I believe Tirzad will be returning to Sumeru City.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: ...Me? Yes, I will. I—I should head back and start writing my paper.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I must... record everything that I witnessed.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But not for academic glory or anything... Jebrael did as he promised he would, yet I... I've always been avoiding my responsibilities.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Now it's my turn. I too must shoulder my responsibilities...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And as for this stone slate...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I've prepared a replica for reference. As for the original... I hope you'll keep it safe for me. I'm not trying to run from danger! It's a commission, you hear it? A commission!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Just think about it. I'll be completely occupied with my paper soon, but an adventurer like you will never stop adventuring, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: If you make new discoveries during this time... Wouldn't we make the perfect team? The thesis material shall be mine, and the Mora yours...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: That's perfect! We'll be making the best use of all our resources!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Jeht... What do you plan to do now? Do you have any friends you can rely on or something?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father... He was so busy, he never had the time for anything... He didn't leave anything behind, just that axe he always used...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father said he hoped he could meet her again in the Eternal Oasis... He said that day was still very, very far away... Liar! He lied to me, and to my mother...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: He should keep his own promise! Now I have to fulfill it for him, and... take his axe and mother's research notes, which he kept with his luggage...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: ...To the Eternal Oasis. I hope they'll find true peace there.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: ...Bee-eep!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there anything we can do to help?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Thank you, but... it's alright. While I was taking a quick look through my mother's research notes, I noticed what seemed like casual diary entries on the edges of the pages.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I found out that my father is from this tribe called "Tanit"... So, I plan to look for them... Perhaps they can tell me about my father...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Sorry, I just... I haven't... I'm sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's give her a moment to herself.

dialogues.speaker: Bonifaz
dialogues.text: Yeah... Anyway, Nachtigal and I will be staying here for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: We'll think long and hard about our future...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should be staying in Sumeru for some time too... Paimon just has this feeling that there are so many more secrets to uncover.

dialogues.speaker: Bonifaz
dialogues.text: Come to us if you need anything. We'll do our best to help you.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: And good luck in your adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: *cough* Nachtigal's invigorating drinks really are strong. If you sat me down at a table now, I'm certain I could write a million words in one go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #The door is shut! {NICKNAME}... What do we do?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: We must defeat Samail, who has stolen Al-Ahmar's power. But his physical form in this world must've been destroyed already...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So that makes him formless... Then how can we defeat him? Don't tell me he's invincible in the Eternal Dreamland...?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: U—Unless someone goes to where he is...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Unless someone stops and defeats him in the Eternal Dreamland... I must... I must protect you...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father! B—But how are you going to come back? Didn't you say that no one can move freely between the Eternal Dreamland and reality?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: There's no time to lose. I promised to keep you safe, until the end... I can't let you all die here!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: What is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Jebrael! Haha, you're here!

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: I knew it... I knew it! We are the twin blades of Thutmose, our lives dedicated to uncovering the secrets of the Golden Slumber...

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: You took the long way around, but it doesn't matter anymore. We've met again here, at the end of that path.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: You were just lost before, but the sands of the Thutmose always return before Al-Ahmar's throne!

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Like the dehydrated thirst for a spring, only the illusion of the Eternal Oasis can relieve our agony...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: I'm inside... the Golden Slumber promised by Al-Ahmar?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Oh... You are not "us" yet.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: ...It's fine. Soon, there'll be no "you." "You" will become a part of "us." This meaningless talk will be unnecessary then.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: No, no! I'm here to stop you! My mission is to protect... I must protect Jeht and the others...

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Why? Why care about such trivial matters? Great power is right before you, it's like a torrent in the desert. Don't you feel it?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: You should obey. Al-Ahmar's will is our will. The Thutmose's dreams are our dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: No! Ufairah taught me that I'm not just some part of you, I'm an independent person! I have my own dreams... I won't go back!

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Jebrael, why don't you understand? Love is just a fever. I even eliminated the infection for you. Has the heat made you lose your mind?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: You're the one who's lost their mind, Samail, not me. The Golden Slumber that Al-Ahmar promised us isn't like this... It's not a sad place with only "we" and no "I."

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: I'm not sad. I know what I want. My dream is to be one with the Thutmose.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Yet you, the warmth of another... I despise such feelings. It makes you weak.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Your betrayal was like a blade in my chest. But I obtained Al-Ahmar's wisdom, and that wound I thought would never heal is nothing but a memory now.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: You've realized it too, haven't you? That drowsiness... Al-Ahmar is summoning you into the dream. Stop arguing meaninglessly with me. Come, fall into deep sleep...

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: When you awaken again... No, when "we" awaken again, nothing will be left standing in our way. The Thutmose's dreams will be fulfilled.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: ...No, you're my enemy! My dream is... is...

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: "We" are the dunes, and you are a grain of sand. We are one. You know this.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: No, I'm the "Treacherous Grit"! I abandoned the Thutmose and chose a different path...

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: You took the long way around, but you reached the correct destination. Admit it. This is the dream hidden within your heart.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: ...I wanted to return to this place?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Yes, you did. There is no hatred here, only eternal peace. No bitter salt water, only an endless spring.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Sleep, Jebrael, sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht's Voice
dialogues.text: (...Father! Father!)

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad's Voice
dialogues.text: (H—His body has disappeared. He's not coming back... Jeht...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon's Voice
dialogues.text: (This can't be...)

dialogues.speaker: Jeht's Voice
dialogues.text: (I refuse to believe it! He always keeps his promises! He promised to tell me about my mother... All of you heard him! He wouldn't lie to me! He never lies to me! *sob*...)

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: ...I refuse to yield. Jeht is right. I'm a man of my word. I promised to protect them... until the end!

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: ...I see. Your ties to the mundane inhibit you. Just like that infection, I just have to eliminate them...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad's Voice
dialogues.text: (...The door is open? It must be Jebrael! It's still shaking, Jeht! It's dangerous here! We can't stay, or else his sacrifice would mean nothing...)

dialogues.speaker: Jeht's Voice
dialogues.text: (Leave if you want! Father... Father will be back. He'll be so sad if he couldn't find me when he wakes up... I won't leave him!)

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Hmph! How foolish! But these trivial troubles will vanish with the wind soon.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: I won't let you win!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Haha! I finally get it... Samail, you're right. There will be no "me," only "us"...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: But you're not the only one who can decide "our" will!

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: You can't be serious...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Samail, the twin blades of Thutmose are equal. So... die here with me!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
Jeht, forgive me. You'll have to go on alone from now on... No, I'm sure you won't forgive me. After all, it's my first time breaking a promise to you.
I hear the voices of many here. I think I hear Ufairah too. She's humming the song of her home.
Oh... If only you could hear it too. Why couldn't I have told you a little more about her? Her soft curly hair... and that innocent smile of hers.
I have so many things I want to share with you, but I'm no longer able to distinguish if they are my memories... or "our" memories...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Afratu
dialogues.text: Who are you? Hah! The researcher and the traitor? Good! Give us the stuff Samail mentioned!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Well, looks like negotiations have broken down!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! We should be able to go to the upper level to see King Deshret's throne now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hurry up, {NICKNAME}! Paimon can't wait to sit on King Deshret's big chair!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Did something that shouldn't be activated get activated?!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Watch out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Strange... Why did they stop?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: King Deshret is as unreasonable as I thought. We've overcome so many trials on our way here! We're "worthy"...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Let's go. Al-Ahmar's throne is higher up — it is close.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yes! That's the big chair! {NICKNAME}, let's check it out!

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: "The dreams of Thutmose... We will fulfill them."

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: It was so hard... so difficult to find all the materials for my paper... Will I never have the chance to record all of this again?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I shouldn't have underestimated superstition...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: (I must make sure that they leave safe and sound...)
